what: kb_get on agent-docs/backend/custom-operations.agent.md with section 'Rules for Custom Operations' returned not found, although kb_search had returned that exact path and heading one call earlier. The builder then read the companion from disk.
why: Index refresh was still running at the time of the search ('results may be stale'), or the section lookup does not match the companion heading. The file exists on disk.
workaround: Read catalog/agent-docs/backend/custom-operations.agent.md from disk (lines 265-272 of custom-operations.md read directly).

what: kb_get on best-practices/backend/generator-ignore-config-protection.md with section 'Practice' returned not found; kb_search later returned the same path, so it is not a missing file.
why: Section name 'Practice' did not resolve; the file exists on disk.
workaround: Retried through kb_search and kb_get on another path; the file itself was not read in this chunk.

what: kb_get on best-practices/frontend/generator-ignore-i18n-layout.md with section 'Practice' returned not found. The path is referenced by a wiki link in the Hungarian page and was never a kb_search hit; the file exists on disk.
why: Section lookup failed on a path that was only reached through a link, not a search hit.
workaround: Gave up on that section; relied on hungarian-full-localization.md instead.

what: kb_get on agent-docs/e2e-testing/README.md with section 'E2E Testing Guide > Key Concepts > Best Practices' returned not found, although kb_search had returned it at hit 3 with the same parent heading.
why: Section lookup failed for a nested heading path in a README.
workaround: Grep of the README from bash (L6343) for the Best Practices list.

what: kb_get on agent-docs/frontend/build-and-deployment.md with section 'Frontend Build and Deployment > Maven Build Modes > Checksum Handling' returned not found; kb_search had returned the same file as hit 3 with the heading 'Checksum Handling'.
why: Full breadcrumb path with a '>' chain did not resolve; the shorter heading would have worked (not tested).
workaround: grep of the file from bash for 'checksum' (L6333).

what: The judo CLI query --select rejected a nested selection (principal{fqn}) with 'not a field of ActorType', while the same field works inside a GraphQL query. Earlier, query --select fqn,principal failed with 'Subselection required' for a transfer-object field.
why: The CLI --select syntax does not accept object sub-selections; the error text does not say so.
workaround: Used judo graphql with an explicit selection set instead (L6299).

what: judo CLI update --schema=<Type> returned 'not a field' for type names (ActorType, Operation) and listed the valid fields of the element, while create --schema=ActorType worked. The meaning of --schema differs between update and create.
why: The --schema option behaves differently per command; update expects a field of the element, not a type name.
workaround: Used the create form and the query command to read the metamodel.

what: kb_get on best-practices/model/initializer-operation.md, section 'Static Initializer Operation for Data Seeding', returned only a keyword line with no procedure text.
why: The section that matched was the :meta chunk (keywords), not the body.
workaround: Recorded as N2 in the re-check; the seeding practice was not read from this page.

what: kb_get on the meta chunk of best-practices/backend/external-api-adapter-pattern.md returned a keyword line only, not the body. The guidance was found in model-blueprints/external-api-adapter-provider-pattern/backend.md instead.
why: The kb returns the :meta chunk (keywords and summary) for some root sections.
workaround: Read the model-blueprint backend.md section 'Backend guidance > The factory'.

what: The kb read-discipline guard fired about six times during CLI, build and generator debugging ('3 consecutive searches without consulting the knowledge base', 'Repeated source searching, still no kb consult'). No kb answer existed for most of those questions.
why: The guard counts shell, grep and jar inspection as source searching, including legitimate build debugging.
workaround: Carried on; ran kb_search only for catalog questions.
proposed_target: kb read-discipline guard (kb_guard_pause or exemptions for build output)

what: judo query with --select on a reference field (principal, output) fails with 'Subselection required for type ESM_TransferObjectType' (or ESM_Parameter). The CLI does not say which subfields to select.
why: The query tool needs a nested selection for reference fields; the CLI help does not show it.
workaround: Read the value with update --brief or with a plain query of the fields that are scalars.

what: The CLI schema says realm applies only when an actor is not anonymous, yet the query shows Customer and Admin with anonymous true and realm webshop.
why: Unclear: either the schema text or the stored actors are inconsistent; the chunk does not settle it.
workaround: None recorded.

what: judo.sh build -a and build -F -KA update ~/.m2 but not application/.karaf/system, so a later start runs stale jars and shows Missing SDK operations. Only a full build fixes it.
why: Build targets write to different locations than the runtime reads; not documented in the help text.
workaround: Full build (build -f -i or full build) after backend changes before starting Karaf.

what: kb_get with a section heading returns only a keyword line or the intro blurb for root sections, not the practice body (correlation-based-event-chaining, reservation-booking-entity Intent).
why: Root sections of best practices and blueprints index only the metadata chunk; the body is in later sections.
workaround: Read catalog files from disk (see c13-11) or use kb_search with other terms.

what: The kb read guard injected a notice about repeated source searching about 30 times during build and test debugging, where no kb entry could answer the question (Playwright logs, Karaf logs, DB queries).
why: Guard counts consecutive non-kb tool calls; debugging a test run is mostly non-catalog work, so the guard fires on normal work.
workaround: Ignored the notice and kept debugging; ran kb_search only for catalog questions.

what: target/judo-cli.jar disappears after a frontend build (build -f -i) and is missing again later; judo update commands fail with Unable to access jarfile until generate-root recreates it.
why: Not stated; build or generate-root removes or does not recreate the CLI jar.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh generate-root, which recreated target/judo-cli.jar.

what: kb_get on a blueprint path returned only the intent paragraph and '(+9 more sections)'; the builder had to read the blueprint files from disk, which a kb-only project cannot do. A bare path without the catalog/ prefix returns 'not found'.
why: kb_get without a section argument does not return the whole short file; the path must use the source prefix.
workaround: Read catalog/model-blueprints/cards-container-configuration-hook/BLUEPRINT.md and related files from disk; logged as R16U-1.

what: The kb read-discipline guard repeatedly printed '[kb] Repeated source searching, still no kb consult' and '3 consecutive searches without consulting the knowledge base' (about 40 times) while the builder ran source greps and test commands. The nudges did not lead to a kb_search.
why: Guard counts shell and grep calls on generated code as source searching, so bulk test work triggers it.
workaround: Ignored the nudges; continued with grep and test runs.

what: Two kb_get calls with a path only (scheduled-data-sync-pipeline and external-system-staging-entity) returned the intro section and '(+7 more sections)'; the builder then read the same catalog files from disk with read and grep.
why: kb_get without a section gives the first section only; the builder did not pass a section from kb_search.
workaround: Read the files from disk.

what: Catalog path check for the abandoned-cart reminder: the builder read osgi-scheduled-background-jobs from disk and then wrote its own cart touch and reminder marker; no kb call for F78 is in the chunk.
why: Same as the general kb skip above.
workaround: Read blueprint from disk.

what: CLI: 'judo create -t MimeType -n json' fails with 'name not defined for MimeTypeCreateInput'. judo-cli.agent.md line 95 says MimeType has no name (type and subType). The builder found it by trial and by grep on disk, not by kb.
why: MimeType create takes type and subType (DEDICATED route addMimeType).
workaround: create -t MimeType --ns webshop -s type=application -s subType=json

what: CLI: 'judo query ui Form' and 'query ui Action' with grep returned no generated form FQNs for the new operations; the builder had to infer names from Table output.
why: Query result for forms is empty or the FQN shape differs from the grep pattern.
workaround: Inferred names from Table and Action output.

what: CLI: 'judo generate' removes target/judo-cli.jar and the CLI is missing until './judo.sh generate-root' is run.
why: generate cleans target; the rule says re-fetch the jar after generate.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh generate-root.

what: judo-cli create -t MimeType -n fails and the doc gives no working form; BinaryType mimeTypes accepts one value per create and --add is rejected too.
why: judo-cli.agent.md lacks the working create form for MIME types; found with create --schema.
workaround: create -t MimeType --ns webshop -s type=application -s subType=json; one MIME type per binary type.

what: kb_get path-only on best-practices and blueprint files returns only the intro line ('(+7 more sections)'); the builder then read the files from disk (gdpr, product-versioning, custom-visual-element-override, data-snapshot-versioning).
why: Same kb_get limit as R17-1: path-only fetch returns the first section of best-practices files.
workaround: Read catalog files from disk.

what: kb_search 'bulk json export actor own data download file' returned a Query Result Methods section, not the export pattern; builder read bulk-json-import-export.md from disk.
why: kb hit not relevant; the right file was only found by a second search.
workaround: Read catalog file from disk.

what: kb_search 'interceptor before after update old values' hit the interceptors Key patterns section; builder then read interceptors.md from disk for two line ranges.
why: kb section did not give the needed body; read from disk.
workaround: Read interceptors.md at offset 144 and 655.

what: create -t MenuItemAccess is refused: the item is created automatically; the CLI suggests create -t Access with --ns and --set target.
why: MenuItemAccess is generated with the TransferObjectType; create route not valid.
workaround: Used update on the auto-created item; label set with update.

what: judo delete --no-check on operations not in each view prints 'error Element not found' for Form and Table but 'removed' for View_Edit.
why: Delete loops over every view type; not all views have the operation.
workaround: Ignored the errors; validate --strict passed.

what: Builder states there is no documented way to declare a database index, so the index part of F80 is not done in the model.
why: The catalog documents it: generator-plugins.md (section Indexes) says the model has no index syntax and to add indexes with a hand-written schema changeset (schema-evolution.md). The builder search did not surface that section.
workaround: Not done (R18-2).
proposed_target: kb_search: index queries did not return the generator-plugins.md Indexes section

what: judo CLI query esm DataMember --select dataType fails with SubselectionRequired for ESM_Primitive.
why: The select needs a sub-selection for a primitive type; the CLI message does not say which field to use.
workaround: Query without the dataType select.
proposed_target: judo CLI query --select on primitive type fields

what: kb_get with path agent-docs/deployment/schema-evolution.agent.md returned a short fragment, and the builder read the best-practice file from disk. In a check, the unqualified agent-docs/ path returned not found; the catalog/ qualified form (as kb_search returns) worked.
why: kb_get path form differs from the path kb_search returns; the fragment did not cover Step 3 fully.
workaround: Read from disk (catalog files).
proposed_target: kb_get path resolution (accept the path form kb_search returns)

what: Builder did not search the kb for the UI validation error ActionContainerSameWithActionDefinition before the build; the catalog entry for it exists in the ui-authoring-guide pitfalls table.
why: kb not consulted for the error text; the kb searches at that point were about reports and xdocreport only.
workaround: Found by build failure.

what: judo.sh build -d (Docker image) failed: rm -rf of the Karaf directory reported Directory not empty while Karaf still ran; a second run said Karaf is not running and exited 1; a third run with -KA exited 1 with no message; no docker image was built.
why: Build script stops Karaf and removes its directory in an order that fails when the process is still alive; the failure exit has no message.
workaround: Compose stack runs the Karaf offline distribution instead (see c17-38).
proposed_target: judo.sh build -d (stop Karaf before rm; clear error exit)

what: mvnd judo-rdbms-schema:help does not exist (only apply, execute and generate goals); builder guessed the help goal.
why: Goal names not checked before use.
workaround: Read the error goal list.

what: After update ImportRunInfo.undo output=UndoMessage, validate passed but the Maven UI build failed with ActionContainerSameWithActionDefinition (the operation form action page container did not match). Running fill on the new TO fixed it.
why: The CLI changes the operation output without creating its UI pages; validate does not run the UI action check that the build runs.
workaround: Ran fill webshop::UndoMessage, then generate-root and generate, then rebuilt.

what: query -s cannot select a reference field: 'Subselection required for type ESM_Class of field target', and input{...} is 'not a field'. --where does not support fqn~ either.
why: CLI query takes only scalar fields; nested references need graphql.
workaround: Switched to judo graphql with nested items { } selections.
proposed_target: judo-cli query (-s nested references) or help text

what: target/judo-cli.jar disappeared after generate or build runs, and every judo call failed with 'Unable to access jarfile'. Builder restored it with generate-root and later copied the jar to /tmp/judo-cli.jar.
why: Generation or build removes target/judo-cli.jar; cause not found.
workaround: Ran generate-root, then used /tmp/judo-cli.jar for later CLI calls.

what: kb_search 'root context redirect default application Karaf servlet / landing' returned only unrelated hits for the question of what the root URL serves and how to change it. Builder concluded there is no documented way.
why: No catalog section answers the root path question directly; the deployment Access Points entry (which says /apps/ lists bundles) was not in the top 5.
workaround: Used curl to check the root and /apps/ and reported no documented change path.
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/deployment/README.md (root path and how to set a default landing)

what: The read-discipline guard fired more than 20 times ('Repeated source searching, still no kb consult'). Builder kept searching the generated source and the .scratch scripts with grep and ctx_search instead of kb_search for JUDO how-to questions.
why: Guard counts bash and ctx_search source lookups as source searching; many lookups were about generated code, which the kb does not index.
workaround: Builder kept going with grep and ctx_search; some lookups were answered by kb_search later.

what: GAPS R19-15 and R19-17 say the catalog documents neither the duplicate-import build error nor the actor order rule. The catalog does document both: catalog/agent-docs/deployment/build-process.md has the section 'Duplicate type imports with a third actor (known issue)' with the create --index 0 workaround.
why: The builder did not search the kb before writing the gap note, so the catalog entry was missed.
workaround: None in this chunk; the GAPS statement stays uncorrected.

what: Adding an Access to the Guest actor also created a MenuItemAccess (Guest::Menu_2, label ShopInfo), which had to be removed by hand after the access was deleted.
why: Unclear; the CLI creates a menu item when an access is added. Not checked in the catalog.
workaround: delete webshop::Guest.shop --cascade removed the menu item as well.
